about: The steps

Leaflegal works in three simple steps. You tell us what you need help with, we introduce you to one regulated firm that handles that kind of matter, and the firm contacts you to talk it through. The whole thing is free for you, and nothing you do on our website commits you to instructing anyone.
This page goes into more detail about each step, what happens behind the scenes and what you can expect from the firm. If you just want to get started, the form takes about two minutes.

about.h3: 1. You tell us what is going on

about: The form starts by asking which area of law your matter falls under. It then asks a handful of questions that are specific to that area. For a house purchase it might ask whether the property is freehold or leasehold. For a driving matter it might ask whether you have a court date. For a business debt it might ask roughly how much is owed and how old the invoice is. These questions are the same ones a firm's intake team would ask on a first call.
At the end you give your name, a mobile number and an email address. You can also add a short note. This is a good place to mention a deadline, a language preference or the best time to call.

about.h3: 2. We check it and introduce one firm

about: When you submit, we check that your enquiry is complete and that it falls within the areas we cover. We then pass it to one regulated firm that handles that type of matter and covers your area. For immigration, we pass it to a regulated immigration adviser. The firm receives your answers and the consent you gave, so it knows you asked to be contacted.

We never pass the same enquiry to several firms. That is a deliberate choice. It means you are not flooded with calls, and the firm that contacts you knows it is the only one introduced to you by us. If you would like to speak to other firms as well, you are free to contact them yourself.

The firm usually contacts you the same working day, most often by phone and sometimes by email or text first. On that first contact it will ask a few more questions, explain whether and how it can help and tell you about its fees. From that point you deal with the firm directly. Leaflegal is not part of your conversations with the firm and does not see the advice it gives.

about.h3: Why one firm and not several

about: Some websites send your details to three, four or more firms at once. That can mean a lot of calls in a short space of time, often from firms that are competing to speak to you first. We think one careful introduction is better for most people. You get a single, focused conversation with a firm that handles your kind of matter, and you keep control over whether you look further.

It also matters to the firm. Because each enquiry goes to one firm only, the firm can afford to spend time on a proper first call rather than racing other firms to the phone. That usually makes for a calmer and more useful conversation.
Before you start
You do not need to prepare anything special before filling in the form. A little thought beforehand can make the first call more useful, though, and help the firm judge how quickly it needs to move.

about.h3: Know roughly what kind of help you need

about: You do not need the legal name for your problem. It is enough to know that you are selling a flat, that you have received a court summons, or that a customer has not paid. If you are not sure which area fits, pick the nearest one and explain in the notes.

Many legal matters have deadlines that cannot easily be moved. Court hearings, reply dates on letters, completion dates, licence renewal dates and dates on immigration letters are all worth noting down. Put the most important one in the form.

Letters, contracts, court papers, notices, invoices and emails all help the firm understand your matter. You do not need to send them through Leaflegal and we do not ask you to upload anything. Just keep them handy for the call. A photo on your phone is usually enough at the start.

It helps to have a rough idea of the outcome you are hoping for, even if it changes once you have spoken to a lawyer. You might want a quick sale, an agreed arrangement for your children, to keep your licence or to be paid what you are owed. The firm will tell you what is realistic in your situation.

Most problems with introductions come from a mistyped phone number or email address. Take a second to check them before you submit. Use a number you will answer, and let the firm know in the notes if there are times when you cannot talk.

about.h3: If your matter involves more than one area

about: Some situations cross over. A separation might involve selling the family home. A business might be owed money and also need help with a licence. If that applies to you, choose the area that feels most pressing and mention the other in the notes. You can also complete the form a second time for a separate matter.

If you are enquiring for a relative, a partner or a business you work for, make sure they are happy for you to do so. The firm will need to speak to the person or business it would be acting for, and it will usually need their own identity documents before it can take instructions.
After you submit
Once you press submit you will see a confirmation on screen. Your enquiry is checked and passed to the firm as soon as possible. Here is what usually happens next.

Your enquiry is recorded together with the consent you gave and the time you gave it. That record is sent to the firm with your answers, so the firm can see that you asked to be contacted about this matter.

The firm calls or emails to introduce itself. If you submit outside office hours, at the weekend or on a bank holiday, the firm will usually be in touch on the next working day. Some firms send a short text or email first so you know who is calling.

The firm asks some questions about your situation, explains how it could help and talks about fees. It may ask you to send copies of documents so it can look at them properly. It will not expect you to make a decision there and then.

If you want to go ahead, the firm sends you its terms of business and confirms its fees in writing. If it is a firm of solicitors, it must also tell you in writing about the fee it pays Leaflegal for the introduction. The firm will also carry out identity checks, which regulated firms are required to do before they act for a new client.

about.h3: If you do not hear anything

about: Check your voicemail, your text messages and your junk email folder. Firms often try more than once. If you still have not heard anything by the end of the next working day, contact us and we will chase it up.

The firm sees the answers you gave, your contact details, the note you added and the record of your consent. It does not see anything else about your visit to our website. If the firm needs more information, it will ask you directly.
The first call
The first call with the firm is a chance for both sides to find out whether they are a good fit. It is not a commitment, and you do not have to agree to anything on the call.

about.h3: What the firm will want to know

about: The firm will usually ask you to explain what has happened in your own words, what stage things are at and what deadlines you are facing. It may ask about the other people involved, so it can check it does not already act for them. That check is called a conflict check and every regulated firm has to do it.

list: Have you dealt with many matters like mine
Who will handle my matter day to day, and what is their role
How do you charge, and what is included
What are the likely next steps and timescales
How will you keep me updated
Is there anything I need to do urgently

about: Some firms give a short amount of general guidance on the first call free of charge. Others prefer to arrange a paid consultation before they look at the details. Both are normal. Ask the firm how it works so there are no surprises.
You can end the call by saying you would like to think about it. A good firm will understand. If there is a deadline coming up, ask the firm how long you have to decide before it becomes a problem.

about.h3: If the call is not convenient

about: If the firm calls at a bad time, it is fine to ask them to ring back later or to arrange a time by email. Many firms can also offer a video call or an appointment at their office if you would prefer to meet in person. Tell them what works for you.

about.h3: If you need support on the call

about: If you would like someone with you on the call, or you need information in a different format or language, let the firm know. Regulated firms are used to making reasonable adjustments, and it helps them to know in advance.
Instructing a firm
Instructing a firm simply means asking it to act for you. Here is what that usually involves once you decide to go ahead.

The firm sends you a client care letter and its terms of business. These explain who will do the work, how fees and billing work, what the firm will and will not do, and how to complain if something goes wrong. Read them carefully and ask about anything that is not clear.

Regulated firms have to confirm who their clients are. You will usually be asked for photo identification and proof of address, and sometimes information about where money for a transaction is coming from. Many firms use an online identity check that you can complete on your phone.
Some firms ask for a payment before they start, which is held towards their fees or disbursements. Others bill at set stages. The firm will tell you what it needs and when.

From here on you deal with the firm directly. Keep copies of everything you send and receive, reply promptly to requests for information and tell the firm straight away if something changes. If you are unhappy with the service, raise it with the firm first. Every regulated firm must have a complaints procedure.

Once you are introduced, Leaflegal steps back. We do not manage your matter or see your files. We are still happy to hear from you if something about the introduction went wrong, or if a firm did not treat you fairly.

about.h3: Costs and how Leaflegal is paid

about: Leaflegal is free to use. The firm pays us a fee for the introduction, and that fee does not change what the firm charges you. Solicitors must tell you about it in writing. The firm's own charges, and any disbursements such as court or search fees, are agreed between you and the firm in its terms of business.
Who it is for

Leaflegal is for people and businesses who are looking for paid help from a regulated lawyer in one of the eight areas we cover. Six of those areas are for matters in England and Wales. Trademark and immigration introductions are available across the UK.

faqs: The form
How long does the form take?

Most people finish it in about two minutes. It is a short set of multiple choice questions about your matter, followed by your contact details. There is an optional notes box if there is something the firm should know straight away, such as a hearing date or the best time to call you.
Why do you ask so many questions about my matter?

The questions help us introduce a firm that actually handles your type of matter and covers your area. They also mean the firm knows the basics before it calls, so you do not have to repeat everything from the start. They are similar to the questions a firm would ask on its first call.
Do I need to upload documents?

No. We do not ask you to upload anything. Keep your documents handy for the first call. The firm will tell you which ones it needs to see and how to send them securely once you have spoken and decided to go ahead.
Can I save the form and come back later?

The form is short, so it is designed to be completed in one go. If you are interrupted, you can simply start again. Nothing is sent to a firm until you have reached the end, given your consent and pressed submit.
What should I put in the notes box?

Anything that will help the firm call you at the right time and understand the urgency. Deadlines, court dates, completion dates and dates on letters are the most useful. You can also mention if you would prefer email or if there are times when you cannot talk.
Can I use the form on my phone?

Yes. The form works on phones, tablets and computers. It is designed to be quick to complete on a small screen, and it works with a keyboard alone and with screen readers. If you have any trouble using it, email us and we will help.
What if I make a mistake on the form?

If you notice a mistake after submitting, such as a wrong phone number or the wrong area of law, email us as soon as you can with the correct details. We will update the firm where we can. If the firm has already called, you can also correct it with them directly.
The introduction
How do you decide which firm to introduce?

We look at the area of law, the type of matter, where you are and anything else you tell us. We then introduce one regulated firm that handles that work and covers your area. We do not pick firms based on who pays us the most, and we do not rank firms for you.
Will more than one firm call me?

No. Each enquiry goes to one firm only. We do not sell it to a list or pass it around. If you want more quotes, you can contact other firms yourself. Using Leaflegal does not stop you speaking to anyone else.
Can I ask for a particular firm?

We cannot introduce you to a specific firm of your choosing. If you already know which firm you want, it is usually quickest to contact them directly. Leaflegal is most useful when you do not yet know who to call.
Can I ask for a different firm?

If the introduction has not worked out, contact us and explain what happened. We will look at it and, where we can, try to help. You are also free to look for another firm yourself at any time without any cost or obligation.
Is the firm independent of Leaflegal?

Yes. The firm is a separate business with its own regulator, insurance and complaints procedure. It is responsible for the advice and service it gives you. Leaflegal does not own any law firm and does not tell firms what advice to give.
What happens if the firm says it cannot help?

Sometimes a firm cannot act, for example because it already acts for someone else involved, the deadline is too tight or the matter needs a different specialist. The firm should tell you clearly. You can then contact us or look for another firm yourself.
Do you check the firms you introduce?

We only introduce firms that are regulated for the work they do, for example by the Solicitors Regulation Authority, the Council for Licensed Conveyancers or, for immigration, an approved regulator. You can also check a solicitor yourself on the SRA register before you instruct them.
Does the firm know I found it through Leaflegal?

Yes. The firm receives your enquiry from us, so it knows the introduction came through Leaflegal. That is also why solicitors tell clients in writing about the fee they pay for the introduction. It is all part of being open about how the service works.
Timing
How soon will I hear from the firm?

Usually the same working day during office hours. If you submit in the evening, at the weekend or on a bank holiday, expect to hear on the next working day. The firm will normally call first and may follow up by email or text if it cannot reach you.
My matter is urgent. What should I do?

Say so clearly in the form and put the key date in the notes box. That helps the firm prioritise. If you have a hearing or deadline in the next day or two, you may also want to contact firms directly, because no introduction service can guarantee a call within a set time.
How long will my matter take?

That depends entirely on the type of matter and the people involved. A house purchase, a lease extension, a divorce and a court case all run on very different timescales. The firm will give you a realistic idea once it understands your situation.
How long do I have to decide whether to instruct the firm?

There is no deadline from our side. The firm may need an answer by a certain date if there is something urgent to deal with, such as a reply to a court or a completion date. Ask the firm on the first call how long you have.
Will the firm call me at a convenient time?

Firms usually call during office hours. If you have said in the notes that certain times are better, the firm will try to fit around that. If the first call comes at a bad moment, simply ask them to call back or to email you to arrange a time.
What if I am abroad or in a different time zone?

Mention it in the notes and say how you would prefer to be contacted. Many firms are happy to start by email or arrange a video call. For most areas the matter itself needs to be in England and Wales. For immigration, introductions are available across the UK.
Costs
How much does Leaflegal cost?

Nothing. Leaflegal is free to use. We are paid a fee by the firm we introduce you to. That fee does not change the price the firm charges you, and the firm will explain its own fees before any work starts.
Will the firm charge me for the first call?

The first call to talk about your matter and the firm's fees is normally free. Some firms offer a short amount of general guidance at no cost, while others charge for a full consultation where they look at the details. The firm will tell you before any charge applies.
How will I know what the firm will charge?

The firm will explain its fees on the first call and confirm them in writing before any work starts. Ask whether the fee is fixed or hourly, what is included, what disbursements are likely and whether VAT is included in the figures.
Does the firm tell me it paid for the introduction?

Yes. Solicitors must tell you in writing about any fee they pay for an introduction, and it must not affect the advice they give you. You can read more about how Leaflegal is paid on our how we make money page.
Can I get legal aid through Leaflegal?

No. Leaflegal introduces people who are looking for paid legal help. Legal aid is only available for certain kinds of matter and depends on your circumstances. If you think you might qualify, the legal aid checker on GOV.UK can tell you more and point you to a provider.
Will I be asked to pay anything up front?

Not by Leaflegal. The firm may ask for money on account once you decide to instruct it, usually to cover early disbursements or the first stage of work. It will explain this in its terms of business, and you do not have to pay anything until you have agreed to go ahead.
Your information
Who sees my answers?

We share your answers and contact details with the one firm we introduce you to, and only because you agreed to that on the form. We keep a record so that we can deal with questions and complaints. We do not share the details of your matter with advertisers or data brokers.
Why do you record my consent?

We record the consent wording you agreed to and when you agreed, and send that with your enquiry. It shows the firm that you asked to be contacted about this matter. It also protects you, because it is clear exactly what you agreed to.
Can I stop the introduction after submitting?

Once your enquiry is submitted it is passed to the firm quickly, so it may already have been sent. If you change your mind, tell the firm when it contacts you, or email us and we will let the firm know. There is no charge and no need to explain.
Do you give legal advice during the process?

No. Leaflegal does not give legal advice or immigration advice at any stage. We may ask questions to understand what kind of matter you have, but only so we can introduce the right firm. The firm's lawyers will give you advice about your own situation.
Is my enquiry kept secure?

Your enquiry is sent to the firm securely and we limit who can see it. Once the firm has your details, it is responsible for keeping them safe under its own data protection and confidentiality duties. Our privacy policy explains how we look after your information and how long we keep it.
Can I make a complaint about Leaflegal?

Yes. Email us with complaint in the subject line, explaining what went wrong and what you would like us to do. We acknowledge complaints within three working days and aim to send a full written response within fifteen working days. Complaints about the firm should go to the firm first.
